issues.existing: three golden chalices held aloft and touching
issues.observed: Two goblets, not three. I resolved exactly two bowls, two stems and two feet at the apex, leaning together rim to rim. Four raised forearms converge on them — two hands on the viewer-left goblet and two hands on the viewer-right goblet.
issues.evidence: The apex of the figure group, above all three heads. Enlarged, the silhouette shows one taller/nearer goblet on the viewer-left and one slightly lower goblet on the viewer-right, with four distinct wrists (bangled) gripping them. There is no third bowl, stem or foot anywhere in that cluster, and no occluding mass that could hide one.

uncertainObservations: Cup count: I can resolve only TWO goblet bowls at the apex, yet FOUR raised hands converge on them — two hands per cup. I examined this region enlarged to be sure. If a third cup is present it is completely hidden behind the other two, but I see no third bowl, stem or foot, so I am recording 2.
I cannot reliably count the small discs in the sky; some may be planets, some may be bright nebula knots. Recorded as count null-equivalent with low confidence.
I cannot tell whether the round fruit at the bottom-left are pomegranates, figs or apples.
The warm band at the horizon could be a sunset, a distant lit city, or both; not resolvable.
The centre figure's eyes read as closed but the face is small; this is not certain.
Whether the three figures are joined hand-to-hand as well as at the cups is unclear — the forearms overlap at the apex.
I cannot count the constellation lines or arcs in the sky.

uncertainObservations: Cup count is the weakest point of this read. I can resolve two goblets meeting rim to rim at the top. The center figure's raised hands reach the same point and could be holding a third goblet hidden directly behind the other two, or could be empty. I will not guess; count is recorded as 2 with low confidence.
I cannot count the fruit in the foreground; it is a continuous overlapping heap that runs out of frame.
The small pale spheres in the sky: I can see at least three and possibly four, but several are cut by the frame edge and some may be bokeh/nebula knots rather than bodies. No reliable count.
Whether the center figure's eyes are closed or merely in deep shadow under her tipped-back head is not resolvable.
The structure at viewer-left is read as trees plus slender columns, but it is dark and could be entirely architecture or entirely vegetation.
The warm band at the horizon could be a sunset, a distant city, or firelight; I only record that it is a warm glow.
